stem: In the context of acute otitis externa, where is tenderness most likely to be elicited upon physical examination?

options.text: Just in front of the tragus
The superior-posterior aspect of the auricle
The soft tissue of the earlobe

explanation: Acute otitis externa is a skin infection of the canal, so pressing on the tragus or the front of the canal causes significant pain.
rationale: Pressure on this specific cartilaginous flap at the front of the ear canal is a classic diagnostic sign.

optionExplanations.A: Acute otitis externa is a skin infection of the canal, so pressing on the tragus or the front of the canal causes significant pain.
optionExplanations.B: While a node may drain there, tenderness of the mastoid tip specifically is more likely associated with otitis externa than mastoiditis, which presents higher up.
optionExplanations.C: This area is typically associated with the pain of mastoiditis rather than the external canal infection of otitis externa.
optionExplanations.D: The earlobe does not contain the cartilaginous canal skin that is inflamed in otitis externa.

source.hint: Pressure on this specific cartilaginous flap at the front of the ear canal is a classic diagnostic sign.
